cards.text: This is Solomon, son of David and king of Israel, handing out wisdom two lines at a time (Proverbs 1:1). Most of his sayings flip halfway, with one kind of person and then the opposite. First up: whoever loves discipline loves knowledge, which is like the smoke alarm going off over your cookies and you saying, "Thank you, I needed that."

cards.question: Solomon says whoever loves discipline loves knowledge. What does he call the one who hates correction?

cards.text: The good man obtains favor from the LORD, but the LORD condemns a man who devises evil. Devises, friend, as in not an oops but a whiteboard and a plan.

cards.question: Solomon says a man can be established through wickedness, as long as he's careful.

cards.text: Now Solomon talks marriage. A wife who causes shame is like decay in her husband's bones, and friend, that's not a scratch on the surface, that's trouble ALL the way down.

cards.question: Solomon flips it: a wife of noble character is her husband's crown. What is that picture saying she brings him?

cards.text: Then he looks at what people are planning. The plans of the righteous are just, but the counsel of the wicked leads to deceit, so you ask that crew for advice and you walk out holding a SCHEME.

cards.question: Solomon says the words of the wicked lie in wait for blood, but the speech of the upright ___ them.
Solomon says the wicked are overthrown, but the house of the righteous will stand.
Solomon says a man is praised according to his wealth.

cards.text: Now two men. One is lightly esteemed but has a servant, and friend, somebody once bought me for twenty-five cents, so I KNOW that guy.

cards.question: Solomon says it's better to be lightly esteemed yet have a servant than to be self-important but lack what?
Solomon says a righteous man regards the life of his animal. But the tender mercies of the wicked are only ___.

cards.text: The one who works his land will have plenty of food. It's not glamorous and nobody's throwing him a parade, but that man EATS.

cards.question: Solomon says the one who works his land will have plenty of food. Who does he say lacks judgment?

cards.text: The wicked desire the plunder of evil men, but the root of the righteous flourishes. Crooks are eyeing other crooks' loot, while the righteous just keep on growing.

cards.question: Solomon says an evil man gets trapped while a righteous man escapes from trouble. What traps the evil man?
Solomon says only the work of a man's hands brings him good things, and his words make no difference.

cards.text: Round two. The way of a fool is right in his own eyes, like me swearing I don't need a timer while the smoke alarm screams otherwise.

cards.question: Solomon says the fool thinks his own way is right. What does a wise man do?

cards.text: A fool's anger is known at once. No loading screen, no buffering, just INSTANT.

cards.question: Solomon says a fool's anger shows at once. What does a prudent man do with an insult?

cards.text: Then honesty: he who speaks the truth declares what is right, but a false witness speaks deceit. That's the coworker whose story about the broken copier changes every time somebody new asks.

cards.question: Solomon says speaking rashly is like a piercing sword, but the tongue of the wise brings ___.

cards.text: Here's a line worth framing: truthful lips endure forever. FOREVER, friend, longer than me, my bakery and every cookie I ever stamped.

cards.question: Solomon says a lying tongue lasts only a moment.
Solomon says deceit is in the hearts of those who devise evil, but the counselors of peace have ___.
Solomon says harm follows the righteous wherever they go, while the wicked live free of trouble.

cards.text: Now something the LORD can't stand: lying lips are detestable to the LORD. Not mildly annoying, friend, not a little side-eye. DETESTABLE.

cards.question: Lying lips are detestable to the LORD. Who does Solomon say are His delight?

cards.text: A shrewd man keeps his knowledge to himself, but a foolish heart proclaims its folly. That's the guy who hits reply-all on every single thought he's ever had.

cards.question: Solomon says the hand of the ___ will rule, but laziness ends in forced labor.

cards.text: Then Solomon gets tender: anxiety weighs down the heart of a man. Anybody who's lain awake at 3 a.m. replaying one email knows EXACTLY what he means.

cards.question: What does Solomon say cheers up a heart weighed down by anxiety?
Solomon says a righteous man is cautious in friendship.

cards.text: A lazy man does not roast his game, but a diligent man prizes his possession. The lazy guy gets the game and then just lets it sit, like mixing the dough and never turning on the oven.

cards.question: Solomon ends with two paths, and one of them leads to death. What is in the path of righteousness?

findings.problem: The question asks what a crown says a wife of noble character brings her husband. The wrong answer "Wealth" is too close to the right answer. A crown is a picture of royalty and riches, so a baker could argue that "Wealth" is right alongside "Honor".

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: Proverbs 12:12 says "the plunder of evil men" and doesn't say whose plunder it is. It could be loot taken by evil men or loot taken from them. The card settles it as "Crooks are eyeing other crooks' loot," which picks one meaning the text leaves open.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: This story card is three sentences: "Now something the LORD can't stand: lying lips are detestable to the LORD." / "Not mildly annoying, friend, not a little side-eye." / "DETESTABLE." Only the opening card may run to three sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Proverbs 12:8 is covered only by a false statement: "a man is praised according to his wealth." No card ever says that the right word is wisdom, or that a twisted mind is despised. The baker can't reason out "wisdom" from a false-true pick, so the verse's key point may never reach them in Prep. The same pattern leaves parts of other verses untold: "the righteous cannot be uprooted" (Proverbs 12:3, stop 1 card 4) and "the ways of the wicked lead them astray" (Proverbs 12:26, stop 2 card 17).
findings.question: Does the reaction screen after a pick (answer-explanations.md) show the true wording of the verse? Or must Prep's own cards tell the key content of a verse whenever a true or false card is written as a false statement, so the passage isn't missing an important detail?
